name: Cost Per Wear Math
why_it_works: Sticker price is the only number most shoppers see. Dividing price by real uses reframes an expensive item as the cheaper one, and because the viewer can check the math on their own fingers, it feels like their conclusion, not a sales pitch.

hook.pattern: Lead with a price comparison that looks wrong, then prove it with simple division.
examples: The {{cheap_price}} {{product}} costs more than ours. Here's the math.
Cheap {{product}} vs ours, divided by how often you use it.
Price tag lies. Cost per use doesn't.

craft.notes: Slide 1 must state a claim that sounds backwards so people swipe to check it. Put the division on its own slide so the reveal of the per-use numbers feels like a payoff. Use conservative use counts so the math survives skeptics in the comments.

do_not: Inflate your own lifespan numbers; use the low end you can defend
Show or name a real competitor's product or packaging
Bury the per-use numbers in small text; they are the whole post
compliance: Supplements: compare cost per serving only; make no health, cure or treatment claims, and add 'These statements have not been evaluated by the FDA' if any benefit is mentioned
Skincare: no medical claims (treats, cures, heals); results language must be cosmetic and typical
Every price and lifespan number must be accurate and current at posting
